stories.title: Webb Captures Stellar Jets
stories.summary: Infrared images from the James Webb Space Telescope show many young stars and still-forming protostars inside the star-forming cloud NGC 7129. The picture separates warm hydrogen in single-atom form from cooler hydrogen bound into molecules, which jets from buried protostars have struck and heated. Such observations help astronomers study how collapsing gas clouds give rise to new stars.

stories.title: Infrared light overcomes mirror coating obstacle in gravitational wave detector upgrades
stories.summary: Researchers have developed and tested a new locking method for gravitational wave detectors that will advance the discovery of distant black holes and neutron stars colliding.

stories.title: From spin wave to superconducting circuit: A one-way street for quantum information
stories.summary: Scientists at Argonne National Laboratory and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign have shown a way for information to travel in only one direction, from a spin wave in a magnetic material to a superconducting circuit. Spin is a quantum property of particles that can store and process information. Controlling the direction of this signal flow could help magnetic materials become useful parts of future quantum computers, sensors and secure communication systems.

stories.title: Optical skyrmions can control the motion of magnetic skyrmions
stories.summary: Researchers report that patterns of light called optical skyrmions can be used to steer magnetic skyrmions, which are tiny swirls of magnetisation inside some magnetic materials that act much like particles. Because these swirls are very small and need little energy to move, they could carry information in low-power memory and logic devices. Precise control of their motion has been a major goal, so this approach links light and magnetic fields in a potentially useful way.

stories.title: Scientists may have found a shortcut to fusion energy
stories.summary: Researchers at Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory have calculated that a fusion reactor might reach ignition more easily if its plasma is heated first and only then made denser, rather than the usual order. This reversed approach could let future reactors become self-sustaining while using much less energy and avoiding problems that make ignition harder. Fusion requires high temperature and density so that nuclei can overcome electrostatic repulsion and fuse.

stories.title: Fastest star in the Milky Way feels the rotation of our central black hole
stories.summary: The Milky Way’s massive black hole is rapidly rotating, and a star in an unprecedentedly close orbit could help measure its spin
